_comment: Florida funeral-cost survey. Prices are what providers publish online, gathered from search results on 2026-11-07 (pages were not opened directly). verified stays false until every price is re-checked on the provider's own page; scripts/check-publish.mjs blocks launch until then. Local facts carry their own sources.

wait48.text: Florida law bars cremation until 48 hours after death.

metros.area: Orange, Seminole, Osceola and Lake counties
metros.intro: Orlando-area families have a lot of choice. We found published prices from eight funeral homes and cremation providers across Orange, Seminole, Osceola and Lake counties. Direct cremation is the easiest service to compare, and even there the spread is wide.

me.name: District 9 Medical Examiner (Orange County, also serving Osceola)
me.feeText: $60 for each cremation approval, effective October 1, 2025
me.note: Local price lists also show $60 for Seminole and Lake counties; we could not confirm those on an official page.

deathCert.office: Florida Department of Health in Orange County

cemeteries.name: Cape Canaveral National Cemetery
cemeteries.note: VA listings differ on whether casket burial is currently available, so call 321-383-2638 first.

program.name: Orange County Public Burial & Cremation Program
points: Run by Orange County Health Services: 407-836-2642.
The closest relative or the legally responsible person applies, and the application must be notarized.
The county's standard is cremation; ask about burial.
The ashes must be picked up or shipped within 30 days, and the program does not pay for shipping.
Ask about the income rules. We could not confirm them on an official page.

metros.intro: Tampa had the lowest middle price for direct cremation of the four metros we checked. The catch is the medical examiner's approval fee: Hillsborough County doesn't publish it where we could find it, and local price lists disagree.

me.name: District 13 Medical Examiner (Hillsborough County)
me.feeText: Not published where we could find it. Local price lists show $50 or $75
me.note: The county posted a change to its medical examiner fee ordinance in May 2026, so ask the provider for the current amount.

deathCert.office: Florida Department of Health in Hillsborough County

cemeteries.name: Florida National Cemetery
cemeteries.place: Bushnell, about 50 miles north of Tampa

cemeteries.name: Sarasota National Cemetery
cemeteries.note: Open for casket and cremation burials.

cemeteries.name: Bay Pines National Cemetery
cemeteries.note: Cremated remains only for new burials.

metros.programNote: We didn't find a Hillsborough County program that pays for burial or cremation for low-income families. The county's policy for unclaimed remains makes cremation the default, and relatives who want a burial are pointed to agencies that help with burial costs.

metros.intro: For veterans and their spouses, Jacksonville National Cemetery changes the math: for eligible families the VA provides the grave, the opening and closing, the liner, the headstone and perpetual care at no cost. Funeral home and cremation charges are still the family's to pay.

me.name: District 4 Medical Examiner (Duval County)
me.note: Set by a 2014 city ordinance, the newest official schedule we found; a 2025 local price list shows the same $50.

deathCert.text: $15 for the first certified copy and $10 for each additional copy
deathCert.office: Florida Department of Health in Duval County

cemeteries.name: St. Augustine National Cemetery
cemeteries.note: Closed to new burials; only existing family graves.

program.name: City of Jacksonville Indigent Cremation Program
points: Run by the Social Services Division. It covers cremation only.
Eligibility depends on income, assets and ability to pay for private arrangements.
Apply through the Emergency Financial Assistance line: (904) 255-2469.
Bring photo ID, Social Security documents for the household, and proof of household income and resources.
If an application is denied, there is a 90-day wait before a new appointment.

metros.intro: Miami-Dade's medical examiner charges $75 to approve a cremation, the highest official fee among the counties we checked. The county also runs one of the most detailed help programs for families who cannot afford a cremation.

deathCert.text: $20 for the first certified copy and $16 for each additional copy ordered at the same time
deathCert.office: Florida Department of Health in Miami-Dade County

program.name: Miami-Dade Medical Examiner Indigent Cremation Services
points: The death must happen in Miami-Dade County, and the person applying must be the legally authorized person.
Household income should not be above the federal poverty guidelines.
Basic cremation only: no embalming, viewing or memorial, and no help once the body has gone to a funeral home.
County fees from October 1, 2025: $475, or $150 with proof of SNAP, Medicaid, SSI or TANF.
It can take eight weeks or more.

extra.text: The medical examiner also publishes a list of low-cost funeral homes and crematories. It does not endorse them.
